h1:
5 Short-Stay & Day-Use Hotels
in Sukhumvit Bangkok
Clean, Private & Bookable
heroSub: True drive-in man rood motels are now rare inside the Sukhumvit core, but the need for private, clean short-stays hasn't gone anywhere. We've rounded up 5 honest options — from officially bookable day-use in a 4-star Ascott property with a rooftop infinity pool, to a theatrically designed boutique with private parking, an hourly hotel steps from the MRT, and the one classic drive-in motel that's still out here.
heroStats: ✅ Honest takes from real reviews for every stay
introH2: 🏙️ What short-stay options are there in Sukhumvit, and how do you choose the right one?
introHtml: The classic man rood — a drive-in motel where you pull straight into your own curtained garage, never pass a lobby, and pay in cash by the hour — has almost vanished from inner Sukhumvit. Land costs too much. But the need for private, clean, discreet short-stays hasn't gone anywhere; it's simply shifted shape. Today Sukhumvit offers four cleaner, more honest alternatives: hotels and serviced apartments that officially list day-use packages on Dayuse.com (book online, get a receipt, check in like any other guest, no awkwardness); boutique design hotels in Thonglor with private parking out front; genuine hourly-rate hotels walking distance from the MRT; and, at the far end of the Ekkamai soi, one surviving old-school drive-in that still does things the original way. This article covers all 5, reviewed in depth — the good, the honest caveats, and the exact booking path for each.
mrtHtml: The Sukhumvit strip covers several BTS and MRT stations. The 5 properties in this article are spread from Sukhumvit Soi 13 (near BTS Nana/Asok) to Sukhumvit 22 (350 m walk to MRT Queen Sirikit) to Thonglor/Soi 55 (near BTS Thonglor) and out to Sukhumvit 71/Ekkamai (free shuttle to BTS Phra Khanong/Ekkamai). All are accessible by car — key for the short-stay category. The day-use properties (Somerset, Citrus) work perfectly without a car; PlayHaus and V One Pride suit drivers; Tong Kao is drive-in only.

entries.storyHtml: Somerset Sukhumvit 71 Bangkok is a 4-star serviced apartment by Ascott that opened in late 2024 — every room still feels new — and it's the cleanest, highest-standard day-use option in this article. The headline fact: day-use is officially available through Dayuse.com, from about ฿1,400 (a 58% discount off the nightly rate), bookable with a credit card, a receipt is issued, and you check in exactly like any other guest, with full access to the 15th-floor infinity pool and the Sol & Luna restaurant with its Bangkok skyline panorama. What you need to know honestly: the location is in the quiet Ekkamai residential zone, about 3 km from the nearest BTS — you'll need the free shuttle or Grab every time you want to leave. And soundproofing between rooms is a recurring complaint in reviews; request a corner room or a high floor if noise matters to you.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Day-use must be booked through Dayuse.com directly — not via Agoda or Booking.com. If you're staying overnight, hit the rooftop at 17:00–19:00 for the golden-hour skyline view before you check out.
pros: Officially bookable day-use via Dayuse.com — receipt, no questions, credit card accepted
15th-floor rooftop infinity pool and Sol & Luna restaurant with genuine 360° city views

cons: About 3 km from BTS — you depend on the free shuttle or Grab for every trip out

No in-room washing machine · some minor hidden charges (e.g. laundry bag fee) noted in reviews

entries.storyHtml: Citrus Sukhumvit 13 Nana Bangkok is a 3-star hotel with 79 rooms on Sukhumvit Soi 13, fully renovated in late 2024–early 2025, and the most-reviewed property in this article — 1,778 reviews on Booking.com at 8.6, which says most guests got what they expected. Day-use is officially listed on Dayuse.com, 10:00–18:00, including access to the rooftop pool; you check in like any other guest, no awkward moments. BTS Nana is 650 m away, but the free shuttle to BTS Nana, BTS Asok, and MRT Sukhumvit takes care of that. The honest caveat: the entry-level Premier Room at 22 sqm feels tight for two people with luggage — upgrade to the Corner Room or above if space matters to you.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Day-use bookings on Dayuse.com usually have free cancellation — lock in a rate early. Use the free shuttle rather than walking 650 m in Bangkok's midday heat.
pros: Official day-use via Dayuse.com, 10:00–18:00, includes rooftop pool access

entries.addr: 205/22-23 Sukhumvit Soi 55 (Thonglor), Khlong Tan Nuea, Watthana, Bangkok 10110
entries.storyHtml: PlayHaus Thonglor is a small 19–20-room boutique hotel in the middle of Thonglor, where each floor is designed around a different theatrical theme — Romeo & Juliet, Mary Poppins, Aladdin, and the Thai historical drama Si Phaendin. What earns it a place in this short-stay list is its free private parking out front — a genuine rarity in Thonglor — plus the high degree of privacy that comes with a 19-room hotel where staff remember your name. The Behind the Scene cocktail bar downstairs is a bonus that reviews consistently praise. The honest side: the rooms are mini-sized and designed for atmosphere rather than square footage, so don't come expecting a spacious suite. Some walls let sound through. And hourly rates aren't published online — call directly to ask.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request your preferred theme when booking. The top-floor Si Phaendin room is the quietest in the building. Grab to BTS Thonglor is 3–5 minutes if you don't want the 10-minute walk.

entries.storyHtml: V One Pride Sukhumvit 22 is a 27-room hotel on Sukhumvit Soi 22 that handles genuine hourly short-stays while sitting in the actual heart of central Sukhumvit — not out in the suburbs. The combination that makes it work: free in-building parking (drive in, park, go straight to your room), plus a 350 m walk to MRT Queen Sirikit, meaning it works for drivers and non-drivers alike. A 3-hour rate starts at around ฿500, though this typically doesn't show on OTA platforms — call the hotel directly to confirm before you drive over. Reviews consistently praise the clean rooms, big comfortable beds, friendly staff, and strong value for the location. The honest note: rooms facing the main road pick up traffic noise; always request an inward-facing soi room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The 3-hour rate is confirmed by phone only — call before you come. Always request a room facing inward (toward the soi, not the main road) — the noise difference is significant.

entries.addr: 70/1 Sukhumvit Soi 63 (Ekkamai 4), Phra Khanong Nuea, Wattana, Bangkok 10110
entries.storyHtml: Tong Kao Hotel — also known as Rong Raem 999 — is a 3-floor, roughly 15-room classic drive-in motel on Ekkamai Soi 4 that still operates exactly as the original format intended: you drive into your own curtained private space beside your room, without passing a lobby or another person. This is the experience that has largely disappeared from inner Sukhumvit; Tong Kao is one of the last examples still running in this part of town. It is genuinely old-school and should be approached as such — basic fittings, no pool, no breakfast, no OTA presence. You must phone ahead: 02-391-1783. No online booking exists. Current rates are not published anywhere; they're in the hundreds of baht per visit. If you're driving in and want the highest degree of entry/exit privacy at the lowest price, and you know exactly what you're looking for, this is your answer.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Always call before driving over to confirm a room is free and get the current rate — 02-391-1783. Use Google Maps searching 'Tong Kao Hotel' or 'Rong Raem 999 Ekkamai' for accurate navigation into Ekkamai Soi 4.
pros: Drive directly into your own private curtained garage — the highest privacy of any option here
Cheapest in the article by a wide margin — rates in the hundreds of baht
576 m walk to BTS Ekkamai, so it's not isolated if you need public transport
cons: No online reviews available — impossible to independently verify current cleanliness or condition
Basic old-school fittings — no pool, no breakfast, no hotel amenities

faqTitle: FAQ — Short-Stay & Day-Use Hotels in Sukhumvit Bangkok

faq.q: Is short-stay or day-use at a Bangkok hotel legal and normal?
faq.a: Yes. Day-use is a completely legal, mainstream hotel service — the hotel officially accepts guests for daytime use of a room, often at a discounted rate compared to a full overnight stay. Both Somerset Sukhumvit 71 and Citrus Sukhumvit 13 are registered on Dayuse.com, a reputable international platform. You book online, pay with a credit card, receive a receipt, and check in exactly like any other guest. This is not the same as an illegal short-time establishment — it's a hotel room for a few hours in the middle of the day.

faq.q: Which property in this article is the cleanest and safest?
faq.a: Ranked by verified review scores: Somerset Sukhumvit 71 scores 9.2/10 for cleanliness — brand-new rooms opened in late 2024, Ascott standard throughout. Citrus Sukhumvit 13 scores 8.9/10 for cleanliness from 1,778 Booking.com reviews after a full renovation in 2024–25. PlayHaus Thonglor scores 8.4/10 for cleanliness from 280 reviews. V One Pride scores 7.8/10 — solid but a small number of reviews mention bathroom mold in certain rooms, worth checking on arrival. Tong Kao Hotel has no online reviews to draw on — you'll need to call ahead and judge in person.

faq.q: Which properties can I book online, and which require a phone call?
faq.a: Book online: Somerset Sukhumvit 71 (overnight via Agoda/Booking/Trip; day-use via Dayuse.com) · Citrus Sukhumvit 13 (same) · PlayHaus Thonglor (overnight via Agoda/Booking/Trip) · V One Pride Sukhumvit 22 (overnight via Agoda/Booking/Trip). Phone only: Tong Kao Hotel (999) — call 02-391-1783; no OTA presence at all. V One Pride's hourly rate also needs direct phone confirmation as it usually doesn't appear on booking platforms.

faq.q: Which place has the most privacy — especially for couples arriving by car?
faq.a: Judged by 'drive in, park, and go straight to your room without passing anyone': Tong Kao Hotel wins clearly — each room has its own curtained private garage. V One Pride Sukhumvit 22 has free in-building parking, with a quiet side-soi entrance and a fast check-in process. PlayHaus Thonglor has free parking out front and only 19 rooms, so it never feels busy. Somerset and Citrus both have free parking but are larger properties with more foot traffic.

faq.q: What is the difference between a day-use, an hourly short-stay, and a classic man rood motel?
faq.a: Day-use = a defined daytime window (typically 10:00–18:00), bookable in advance online at a fixed price — the hotel model. Hourly short-stay = more flexible, billed by time blocks (e.g. 3 hours), often requires a direct call rather than an online booking — the V One Pride model. man rood (drive-in motel) = you drive straight into a curtained private space, pay on arrival or by the hour, no online system — the Tong Kao model. All three are legal in Thailand.

faq.q: Which short-stay option in Sukhumvit is easiest to reach by public transport?
faq.a: Measured by walking distance to the nearest station: V One Pride Sukhumvit 22 is closest — 350 m walk to MRT Queen Sirikit. Citrus Sukhumvit 13 is 650 m from BTS Nana (free shuttle bridges the gap well). PlayHaus Thonglor is about a 10-minute walk or a 3-minute Grab to BTS Thonglor. Tong Kao Hotel is 576 m walk to BTS Ekkamai. Somerset Sukhumvit 71 is the furthest from a BTS station (~3 km), though the free shuttle runs regularly to both BTS Phra Khanong and Ekkamai.
